judge: Claude Code subagent, Claude Opus 5.5, fresh

items.label: A
items.critique: The bounty and '500 in gold' fit Nox, but the speaker in the thanks is someone new who explains why he arrived. The 'young sir' said three times reads like a writer imitating the address rather than using it.

items.label: B
items.critique: The panicked plea and short thanks are Nox-shaped. 'Almost all of the maidens' and the Ogre-dungeon journal feel like a compact pastiche of the campaign's Ogre episodes.

items.label: C
items.critique: The over-the-top 'airborne demons from the underworld' and 'Nox's vital interests' are close to Westwood's comic bombast. A two-sentence journal with an exact count is unusual, but it may be original.

items.label: D
items.critique: The 'mate' tic, 'damn fine spell' and a loose run-on journal sentence. This is Westwood's loose comic register.

items.label: E
items.critique: 'Laying their filthy paws on our belongings', 'Well done, lad!' and '100 in gold!' A plain shopkeeper quest in the original voice.

items.label: F
items.critique: The mentor's grumbling, the robe found in place of the apprentice, 'Hmmm... Yes.', and a scene-ending teleporter instruction. This is the campaign's chapter-opening structure.

items.label: G
items.critique: Very short and vague ('that evil one', 'both items'), which could be Westwood. The 'Regain' journal verb is slightly off-pattern.

items.label: H
items.critique: 'Worse than the pox!', charming the spiders, and the reward of a new title plus free passage. This fits Westwood's chapter-gate quest exactly.

items.label: I
items.critique: The frog and the 'Loads and loads of money?' gag are very Westwood in spirit, but the joke is set up a little too neatly, which could be a pastiche of Nox humour.

items.label: J
items.critique: The quest is given with a key ('ruby key'), 'aggravated the bats' and a signed petition as the reward. Plain, functional and slightly clumsy in the original way.

tells: This packet was hard: nearly every text uses Westwood's plain plea, then short thanks, then imperative journal. The calls on the generated side are low confidence.
I leaned towards 'generated' when a text used Nox signatures ('young sir', a comic money gag, monster bombast) a little more often or more neatly than they tend to occur.
Westwood's quests tie into the chapter's progression (a petition, a title, a teleporter, the Captain waiting). Free-standing favours with only gold as the reward read as less anchored.
Journal verbs off the usual set (Retrieve, Rescue, Kill, Bring ... to justice), such as 'Regain', were taken as a weak cue.
